blog_summary: The blog post discusses the paper 'Distributed deep neural networks over the cloud, the edge, and end devices' by Teerapittayanon et al., which introduces DDNNs—a system for partitioning deep neural networks across cloud, edge, and end devices. Unlike prior work (e.g., Neurosurgeon), DDNNs enable static partitioning while supporting multi-device input aggregation and early classification exits at lower network tiers if confidence thresholds are met. The author highlights the novelty of aggregating inputs from geographically distributed devices (e.g., cameras) and the efficiency gains from early exits, which reduce latency and communication overhead. The paper also leverages binarized neural networks (BNNs) for embedded devices and BranchyNet’s confidence-based early exits. The evaluation demonstrates improved accuracy, lower latency, and fault tolerance compared to cloud- or device-only processing.
paper_title: Distributed deep neural networks over the cloud, the edge, and end devices
paper_abstract: —We propose distributed deep neural networks (DDNNs) over distributed computing hierarchies, consisting of the cloud, the edge (fog) and end devices. While being able to accommodate inference of a deep neural network (DNN) in the cloud, a DDNN also allows fast and localized inference using shallow portions of the neural network at the edge and end devices. When supported by a scalable distributed computing hierarchy, a DDNN can scale up in neural network size and scale out in geographical span. Due to its distributed nature, DDNNs enhance sensor fusion, system fault tolerance and data privacy for DNN applications. In implementing a DDNN, we map sections of a DNN onto a distributed computing hierarchy. By jointly training these sections, we minimize communication and resource usage for devices and maximize usefulness of extracted features which are utilized in the cloud. The resulting system has built-in support for automatic sensor fusion and fault tolerance. As a proof of concept, we show a DDNN can exploit geographical diversity of sensors to improve object recognition accuracy and reduce communication cost. In our experiment, compared with the traditional method of offloading raw sensor data to be processed in the cloud, DDNN locally processes most sensor data on end devices while achieving high accuracy and is able to reduce the communication cost by a factor of over 20x. Keywords-distributed deep neural networks; deep neural networks; dnn; ddnn; embedded dnn; sensor fusion; distributed computing hierarchies; edge computing; cloud computing I.
